source: JPL Horizons API (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api), vector tables, CENTER=500@301, ICRF, KM-S

propagator.frame: Moon-centred ICRF (J2000 Earth-equator axes); km, km/s; time UTC ms

gravity.model: GRGM1200A (GRAIL, NASA GSFC), PDS GRAIL-L-LGRS-5-RDR-V1.0 GGGRX_1200A_SHA.TAB, fully normalised, principal-axis frame

thirdBodies.gm_source: NAIF gm_de440.tpc (BODY399_GM, BODY10_GM; DE440 values, Park et al. 2021)
thirdBodies.positions: astronomy-engine 2.1.19 GeoMoon and HelioVector(Earth), geometric, on a 1 h grid with cubic interpolation

propagator.orientation: IAU/WGCCRE 2009 lunar rotation model (astronomy-engine RotationAxis) then the constant ME->PA rotation of moon_de440_250416.tf (67.8526", 78.6944", 0.2785", axes 3-2-1)
propagator.time: TT = UTC + 69.184 s from 2017-01-01 (naif0012.tls); before 2017 astronomy-engine's Delta-T model
leftOut: lunar and Earth tides (no k2 tide)
propagator.integrator: Gragg-Bulirsch-Stoer, step and order control (Hairer, Norsett & Wanner), relative tolerance 1e-12 on position and velocity, landing on each output node

error_definition.along_km: component of that difference along the Horizons velocity (positive: propagated satellite ahead)
error_definition.late_s: tau minimising |r_propagated(t + tau) - r_Horizons(t)|: the propagated satellite passes the true position tau seconds later (negative: earlier)
error_definition.resid_km: the remaining (radial and cross-track) miss after that time shift

default_on_rule: default_on for the two spacecraft whose Horizons trajectory covers 2026-11-14 and whose propagation holds best against it over 7 days (Chandrayaan-2 0.24 km, LRO 0.98 km)

sats.error_note: The Horizons Danuri trajectory carries an acceleration of about 33 um/s^2 that the model does not have, nearly constant and pointing at the Sun (cosine 0.999; tests/check_prop.js section H); LRO and Chandrayaan-2 show no such term. Its cause is not identified, so Danuri errors grow about 25 times faster than those of LRO.
